declaredIntent.summary: Implement Task 5 per-item WIII publication and rebuildable cache, then independently archive, PR, merge, and close it.

outOfScope: Scheduler, retry, cancellation, workflow-engine, agent-manager, provider transport, credential, release, tag, and provider-configuration behavior.
Linear fact reduction, stale-lock recovery, lifecycle timing, receipt reuse, verification routing, and enforcement threshold changes assigned to later Work Items.

sources.reason: Task 5 delivery boundary and concurrent publication scenarios.
Existing WIII concurrency and CLI coverage.
Task 4 workload protocol and environment-bound evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: Independent writers and readers must avoid a shared index lock while never exposing partial publication or treating the cache as authoritative.

reasons: Concurrent publication semantics and public query behavior require standard verification.

executionDecision.reason: The publication boundary and workload evidence are sourced and locally verifiable.

preReviewWarnings: Review publication-id binding, cache rebuild behavior, concurrent writer isolation, reader consistency, and cursor monotonicity.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Each Work Item publishes an item-local index-entry containing the same publication identifier as its complete snapshot.
A cache loss or deliberately malformed aggregate cache is rebuilt from valid item-local entries without omitting a valid entry.

A concurrent run of 64 distinct Work Items completes without shared-index lock timeout, lost entry, or partial reader result; each reader sees old complete state, new complete state, or explicit inconsistent.
The active-list cursor advances monotonically across complete per-item publications.
Focused/full WIII tests, Task 4 workload comparison, required governance checks, archive, PR, merge, and ai-close-work-item have recorded evidence.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: The current shared aggregate index is rewritten under a global lock, which serializes independent Work Item writers and leaves cache recovery without a per-item authoritative publication unit.
constraints: A single Work Item writer must not acquire a shared aggregate index lock.
A reader may return only an old complete view, a new complete view, or explicit inconsistent; it may not silently omit a valid delta.
The aggregate cache is rebuildable and never authoritative for a single Work Item.
Use Task 4 workload protocol for comparison without treating local measurements as a budget.
Use the recorded user approval only for this Work Item's PR/merge and governed cleanup.
intent.rationale: Per-item immutable publication fragments decouple independent writers and let a damaged cache be reconstructed from complete item-local evidence.

scenarioCoverage.expected: All item-local publications exist without shared lock timeout or lost entry.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused concurrent writer test and Task 4 workload comparison.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Reader runs during a publication replacement.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Reader sees old complete, new complete, or inconsistent; no omitted partial delta.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Aggregate cache is malformed after valid entries exist.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Cache is rebuilt from valid item-local entries and cursor remains monotonic.
